research_question.question: 益生菌补充对成人肠易激综合征（IBS）症状的疗效与菌株特异性
research_question.scope: 人体对照试验与系统综述；结局含 IBS 全局症状/腹胀/腹痛评分

inclusion.text: 人体对照试验或系统综述，结局包含 IBS 症状测量
干预为口服益生菌制剂（单菌株或多菌株）

exclusion.text: 非人体研究（动物/体外/模型）
综述会议摘要与正式发表版本重复，合并保留正式版本
结局不含 IBS 症状测量（如仅代谢指标）

papers.title: Bifidobacterium infantis 35624 improves global IBS symptoms: a randomized controlled trial
papers.abstract: Background: IBS symptoms fluctuate without structural cause. Methods: 77 patients were randomized to Bifidobacterium infantis 35624 or placebo for 8 weeks; global IBS symptom scores were assessed weekly. Results: Patients receiving Bifidobacterium infantis 35624 showed a clinically meaningful reduction in global symptom scores compared with placebo (p=0.02). Adverse events were similar between groups. Conclusion: This strain improves global IBS symptoms in this trial.

papers.title: A multi-strain probiotic formulation reduces bloating in IBS patients
papers.abstract: We conducted a double-blind trial in 120 IBS patients assigned to a multi-strain probiotic or placebo for 12 weeks. Bloating scores decreased significantly in the probiotic group versus placebo (p=0.01), while abdominal pain differences were not significant. The formulation contained lactobacilli and bifidobacteria. Tolerability was good with no serious adverse events.

papers.title: Probiotics are not superior to placebo for overall IBS symptom relief: a controlled trial
papers.abstract: In this randomized controlled trial of 100 IBS patients, a probiotic mixture was compared with placebo for 10 weeks. Overall symptom relief did not differ between groups at week 10 (p=0.31). Subgroup analyses suggested possible benefit for constipation-predominant patients only. We conclude that probiotics were not superior to placebo for overall IBS symptom relief in this sample.

papers.title: Strain-specific mechanisms of probiotics in visceral hypersensitivity: a systematic review
papers.abstract: This systematic review synthesizes human and mechanistic evidence on strain-specific probiotic effects in visceral hypersensitivity. Included trials suggest that effects are strain- and dose-dependent, and that pooling heterogeneous strains may mask strain-specific signals. The review highlights gaps in standardized outcome measures.

papers.title: Gut microbiota modulation reduces visceral pain in a rodent model
papers.abstract: In a mouse model, probiotic administration altered gut microbiota composition and reduced visceromotor responses to colorectal distension, indicating reduced visceral pain sensitivity in rodents.

papers.title: Bifidobacterium infantis 35624 improves global IBS symptoms (conference abstract)
papers.abstract: Conference abstract reporting the same trial as R01: 77 patients randomized to Bifidobacterium infantis 35624 or placebo for 8 weeks with reduced global symptom scores.
